overviewCards.title: Phishing Tackle Box
overviewCards.description: Modern security teams need to have a plan in place to rapidly detect and effectively respond to phishing attacks. A longtime favorite for attackers, it is estimated that phishing attacks account for more than 80% of reported security incidents.

overviewCards.title: Vulnerability and Remediation Toolkit
overviewCards.description: This toolkit helps security and IT collaborate effectively by integrating crucial communications channels like Slack or Microsoft Teams with ITSM solutions such as JIRA. It will also sync your vulnerability data with your patching solutions and make critical risk data easily accessible outside of Vulnerability Management.

overviewCards.title: Ransomware Containment Toolkit
overviewCards.description: Ransomware attacks are especially destructive in an already uncertain environment. Leveraging this toolkit will help lessen the severity of such attacks (or prevent them altogether) by containing, blocking, or reducing privileges to endpoints.

overviewCards.title: Threat Investigation Toolkit
overviewCards.description: Context is everything when working with remote teams to neutralize a threat or resolve and incident. This toolkit can help you enrich your alerts and take action on incidents collaboratively, even in a distributed work environment.

overviewCards.title: Identity and Risk Based Access Toolkit
overviewCards.description: As remote access to critical systems becomes the norm, this toolkit automates key workflows such as provisioning and deprovisioning, updating privileges based on group membership, and disabling or resetting user accounts.

toolkits.title: Phishing Tackle Box
toolkits.description: Modern security teams need to have a plan in place to rapidly detect and effectively respond to phishing attacks. A longtime favorite for attackers, it is estimated that phishing attacks account for more than 80% of reported security incidents.

subTopics.title: Phishing Alerts
subTopics.description: Email is dead. Long live email. Forward alerts and key data points from reported phishing emails to Slack or Microsoft Teams.

sections.sectionCopy: Funnel alerts and enriched indicators directly to Slack or Microsoft Teams for faster detection and action.

sectionItems.name: Get alerts directly in chat with enriched data
Ensure everyone on the team is aware of the same things simultaneously
Move quickly against threats and speed up investigation

workflows.name: Post Office 365 Phishing Alerts to Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: 50% of credentials that are harvested via phishing are collected within the first 60 minutes. This workflow helps speed up your reported phishing review process by pushing alerts and enriched IOCs safely to your team via Slack or Microsoft Teams.

workflows.name: Post Exchange Phishing Alerts to Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: 50% of credentials that are harvested via phishing are collected within the first 60 minutes. This workflow helps speed up your reported phishing review process by pushing alerts and enriched IOCs safely to your team via Slack or Microsoft Teams.

workflows.name: Post Gmail Phishing Alerts to Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: 50% of credentials that are harvested via phishing are collected within the first 60 minutes. This workflow helps speed up your reported phishing review process by pushing alerts and enriched IOCs safely to your team via Slack or Microsoft Teams.

subTopics.title: Indicator Enrichment
subTopics.description: Indicators of compromise (IOCs) are crucial in positively identifying phishing attempts. These workflows extract and enrich IOCs to help you confidently respond to reported phishes.

sections.sectionCopy: Find the information you need about threat indicators using Slack or Microsoft Teams chat commands.

sectionItems.name: Just type in chat to look up an IP address, domain name, hash, and more
Bring visibility to your team's work by seeing progress out in the open
Move quickly against threats and speed up investigation

workflowList.sectionCopy: Indicators of compromise (IOCs) are crucial in positively identifying phishing attempts. These workflows extract and enrich IOCs to help you confidently respond to reported phishes.

workflows.name: Enrich Indicators with OSInt from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Threat Intelligence doesn’t have to come with a cost. This workflow uses open-source intelligence (OSINT) to perform domain lookups, header analysis, hash analysis, and more directly from Slack or Microsoft Teams. Just connect your Chat app (Slack or Microsoft Teams) and activate this instant indicator enrichment workflow.

workflows.name: Enrich URL with VirusTotal from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Roughly 88% of malicious URLs are delivered via email. This workflow reduces human interaction with suspicious links by automatically extracting and analyzing all URLs in a reported phishing email.

workflows.name: Enrich IP with IPStack from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Email header information, like a sender’s origin IP address, can reveal how and from where a malicious email arrived in your inbox. This workflow automates the extraction and geolocation or reputation lookup of an IP address from an email header.

workflows.name: Enrich Hash with VirusTotal from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: While some phishing emails contain links that direct users to malicious sites, others contain attachments that have malware themselves, warranting deeper analysis. This workflow safely extracts file attachment hashes and searches for matches in sandboxing or malware analysis solutions.

workflows.name: Unshorten URL with unshorten.me from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Obfuscated URLs are a favorite tactic for attackers looking to trick users into “watching hilarious cat videos''. This workflow takes an obfuscated or abbreviated URL (eg, bit.ly, tinyurl) and unshortens it, allowing you to lookup the real phishing link.

subTopics.title: Email Remediation
subTopics.description: One phish, two phish, red phish, true phish. Use these workflows to delete phishing emails, find who else may have been targeted, and block the sender.

sections.sectionCopy: Respond to confirmed phishing attempts by removing malicious emails from user inboxes and blocking the point of origin.

sectionItems.name: Use chat commands to search across user inboxes
Use delete flags to remove malicious emails from inboxes
Rapidly respond to phishing threats to minimize user exposure

workflowList.sectionCopy: One phish, two phish, red phish, true phish. Use these workflows to delete phishing emails, find who else may have been targeted, and block the sender.

workflows.name: Find and Delete Office 365 Emails from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Once you’ve positively identified a phish, removing it from the user’s inbox is critical. This workflow searches for an email with specific criteria such as sender, receiver, or subject and provides the option to delete matches from Slack or Microsoft Teams.

workflows.name: Purge Emails in Office 365 from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Understanding the scope of a phishing campaign is critical to ensuring no one in your organization takes the bait. This workflow runs a search from Slack or Microsoft Teams and purges emails across Office 365 or Exchange inboxes.

workflows.name: Block Senders and Domains in Office 365 from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Don’t fall for the same phish twice. This workflow uses a Slack or Microsoft Teams command to block domains and senders in Office 365.

subTopics.title: User Containment
subTopics.description: Compromised user credentials are a common thread through security incidents and breaches across organizations and threat actors. These workflows help you disrupt the attacker’s kill chain by preventing them from using compromised user credentials for infiltration and lateral movement.

sections.sectionCopy: Stop savvy attackers from using their favorite trick, compromised user credentials, with simple chat commands to disable user accounts and force password resets.

sectionItems.name: Use chat commands to disable or reset a target user account.
Keep your team informed of your response actions.
Mitigate the risk of a new threat quickly and confidently.

workflowList.sectionCopy: Compromised user credentials are a common thread through security incidents and breaches across organizations and threat actors. These workflows help you disrupt the attacker’s kill chain by preventing them from using compromised user credentials for infiltration and lateral movement.

workflows.name: Disable User Account in Active Directory from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Disabling a compromised account can limit the scope of an attack and buy valuable time to investigate and contain the threat. This workflow disables a domain account straight from Slack or Microsoft Teams.

workflows.name: Disable User Account in Azure AD from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Disabling a compromised account can limit the scope of an attack and buy valuable time to investigate and contain the threat. This workflow disables a domain account straight from Slack or Microsoft Teams.

workflows.name: Force Password Reset in Active Directory from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Forcing a user to reset their password is a small inconvenience compared to re-imaging their entire system. This workflow helps you act fast by forcing a password reset directly from Slack or Microsoft Teams.

workflows.name: Force Password Reset in Azure AD from Slack/Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Forcing a user to reset their password is a small inconvenience compared to re-imaging their entire system. This workflow helps you act fast by forcing a password reset directly from Slack or Microsoft Teams.

toolkits.title: Vulnerability Management Automation Toolkit
toolkits.description: This toolkit includes dozens of Automation automation workflows designed with the Vulnerability Management user in mind. Help your Security and IT teams collaborate and conquer vulnerability risk by streamlining vulnerability identification, research, ticketing, patching, and exception management with automation.

subTopics.title: Vulnerability Enrichment
subTopics.description: In cyberspace, we may not always know our enemy, but we can understand our weaknesses. These workflows help make vulnerability risk relatable and repairable by providing you with important context about the vulnerability, affected host, associated exploits, and remediation steps.

sections.sectionCopy: These workflows fetch host, vulnerability, exploit, and remediation info from Vulnerability Management, Rapid7's Vulnerability Database, and Rapid7's Attacker Knowledge Base. The details are posted back to the user in a nicely formatted chat message.

sectionItems.name: Lookup a host, vulnerability, or exploit from chat
Receive details on the specified item in a thread
Patch or move on to the next one!

workflows.name: Alert on New High-Risk Vulnerability in Vulnerability Management with Slack or Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Trigger an alert in chat for every newly discovered vulnerability with a CVSS score > 7.

workflows.name: Send Remediated Vulnerabilities Message in Slack or Microsoft Teams from Vulnerability Management
workflows.extendedDescription: Trigger a notiication in chat for every newly remediated vulnerability.

workflows.name: Lookup Vulnerability from Slack or Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Lookup vulnerability details, including CVSS severity, exploitability, and solution steps, from Slack or Microsoft Teams.

workflows.name: Lookup Exploit with AttackerKB from Slack or Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Lookup exploitability details for a specified vulnerability from Slack or MS Teams.

workflows.name: Enrich CVE with Recorded Future from Slack or Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Collect additional vulnerability intelligence to better understand risk and potential impact with Recorded Future.

workflows.name: Lookup Top Remediations with Vulnerability Management from Slack or Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Lookup the top 10 remediation steps for a given host from Slack or Microsoft Teams.

workflows.name: Lookup Vulnerable Hosts with Vulnerability Management from Slack or Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Lookup a vulnerability in Vulnerability Management, find all assets with that vulnerability present, and list those asset details in Chat.

workflows.name: Lookup Host with Vulnerability Management from Slack or Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Lookup host details, including hostname, IP, MAC, OS, last scan date, vulnerability summary, and running services, from Slack or Microsoft Teams.

workflows.name: Most Vulnerable Assets in Sites to Slack
workflows.extendedDescription: Lookup host details, including hostname, IP, MAC, OS, last scan date, vulnerability summary, and running services, from Slack or Microsoft Teams.

workflows.name: Generate CVE Report from Slack
workflows.extendedDescription: Collect information about a given CVE and identify all hosts affected by that vulnerability with a Slack command. The CVS data is printed in a Slack thread.

workflows.name: Lookup Vulnerability with Rapid7 Vulnerability Database
workflows.extendedDescription: Look up a vulnerability with an API request.

subTopics.title: Exception Handling
subTopics.description: Review and approve Vulnerability Management vulnerability exception requests and manage expiring exceptions without leaving the comfort of your chat tool.

sections.sectionCopy: These workflows send new vulnerability exception requests to a Slack or Microsoft Teams channel, where they can be quickly reviewed and either approved or rejected. This enables a highly efficient vulnerability management program when used in tandem with the Vulnerability Intelligence workflows.

sectionItems.name: Submit a vulnerability exception request in Vulnerability Management
Receive details on the exception request in chat
Review, investigate, and approve or reject the exception request in chat

workflows.name: Manage Vulnerability Exception Requests with Vulnerability Management from Slack or Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Receive chat messages to notify and inform Vulnerability Management administrators to new vulnerability exception requests. Use the host and vulnerability intelligence workflows to augment the exception request with salient information from your environment before deciding to approve or reject the request.

workflows.name: Manage Expiring Vulnerability Exceptions with Vulnerability Management and Slack or Microsoft Teams
workflows.extendedDescription: Notify users in chat when vulnerability exceptions are near expiration.

workflows.name: Automate Vulnerability Exception Management in Vulnerability Management
workflows.extendedDescription: Automate vulnerability exception management in Vulnerability Management by approving exception requests for low-risk, low-scope vulnerabilities.

subTopics.title: Solution-Based Ticketing
subTopics.description: Most security teams do not have control over the patching process. Solution-based ticketing is a great way to help colleagues in IT prioritize the right KBs, software updates, configuration changes, etc.These workflows create solution-based tickets and update them on a daily basis with the latest vulnerability data from Vulnerability Management.

sections.sectionCopy: These workflows use the Top 25 Remediations from Vulnerability Management to create new or update existing tickets in an ITSM solution. By default, these workflows run once per day, keeping your tickets in sync with your Vulnerability Management data.

sectionItems.name: Import the appropriate ticketing workflow from the options below
Configure the connections to your Vulnerability Management console and the ticketing tool and activate the workflow
There is no step 3 - your workflow will create tickets and update them daily!

toolkits.title: Ransomware Toolkit
toolkits.description: Once a single system is infected with ransomware, the clock starts ticking before an organization’s entire network is compromised. Arm your team with an arsenal of powerful Automation workflows to contain the spread of ransomware by blocking infected hosts and C&C servers at the firewall, quarantining endpoints as you investigate further, blacklisting malicious processes based on the latest threat intel, and running on-demand AV scans.
